AI Contract Analysis App for Foreign Workers\' Contract Understanding and Rights Protection

Many foreign workers in Korea either do not create employment contracts or, even when they do, cannot understand the content, leading to serious rights violations such as unpaid wages, unfair dismissal, and long working hours.\n\nLawRo is an app that uses AI to automatically analyze employment contracts, helping foreign workers understand their contract content in their native language, recognize violations, and protect their rights on their own.
OCR recognition of employment contracts to check for missing essential items and potential legal violations
Translation and explanation of contract content in user\'s native language for easy understanding
Digital storage of concluded contracts, available for disputes or contract renewals
Real-time consultation for questions about working conditions and legal violations
Work Time Tracking and Salary Calculation
Automatic recording of working hours and support for accurate salary calculations including overtime pay
Intuitive interface that anyone can easily use, even if not familiar with Korean
Which service would you like to use?

• Please register your GPS location accurately when measuring work time
• Use AI chatbot for legal reference only
• Expert review is recommended for contract analysis results
• AI-provided services have no legal effect.
1. Purpose of Personal Information Collection and Use

LawRo processes personal information for the following purposes:

• Member registration and management
• Contract analysis service provision
• Customer consultation and complaint handling
• Service improvement and statistical analysis
• Required information: Name, email address, password\n• Optional information: Workplace location information\n• Automatically collected information: Service usage records, access logs
3. Processing and Retention Period of Personal Information
• Until member withdrawal or retention period specified by law\n• Contract analysis records: 3 years\n• Work time records: 3 years
4. Provision of Personal Information to Third Parties

The company does not provide users\' personal information to external parties in principle. However, personal information may be provided in accordance with relevant laws when required by legal provisions or investigative agencies.

The company consigns personal information processing tasks as follows to provide services:

• AI analysis service: OpenAI
• Cloud service: AWS

Users can exercise the following rights at any time:

• Request notification of personal information processing status
• Request access to personal information
• Request correction and deletion of personal information
• Request suspension of personal information processing
Personal Information Protection Officer\n• Name: TABA 8th Team 3

This privacy policy may be added, deleted, or modified in accordance with changes in laws, policies, or security technologies. Changes will be announced through notices 7 days prior to implementation.

The contract meets basic requirements, but attention is needed for missing important items such as wage calculation and break time.
According to Article 17 of the Labor Standards Act, wage components, calculation methods, and payment methods must be clearly specified, and violations may result in corrective orders for employers.

Article 54 of the Labor Standards Act requires at least 30 minutes of break time for work of 4 hours or more, which must be freely available during working hours. Disputes may occur if not clearly specified in the contract.
Probation periods affect wage deductions and must be clearly specified, as omission may violate workers\' rights.

This contract specifies the basic rights and obligations of workers, but attention is needed for omissions in several important items. In particular, wage components are not specified, making it impossible for workers to clearly understand the composition of their actual wages. This can cause legal disputes, especially for foreign workers where language barriers may lead to misunderstandings. Additionally, break times are not specified, making it unclear whether workers can take sufficient rest. This can directly affect workers\' health and work environment quality. The omission of probation periods affects wage deductions, so failure to clearly specify this may violate workers\' rights. While this contract meets minimum wage requirements, workers\' rights may not be sufficiently protected due to these omissions. Therefore, when creating contracts, it is necessary to use standard employment contract forms and provide specific details reflecting actual working conditions for each item. Particularly, multilingual notation and visual explanations for foreigners would help prevent legal disputes.

The employment contract has several issues including unspecified probationary period and wages, and no break time mentioned. However, it complies with minimum wage and basic working conditions are specified, requiring attention.
Probationary period and wages not specified
Foreign worker accommodation type and meal costs not specified
Obligation to specify probationary period and wages
According to Labor Standards Act Article 17, probationary period and wage composition and calculation method must be clearly specified.
According to Labor Standards Act Article 54, at least 30 minutes of break time must be provided for 4 hours of work.
According to the Act on Foreign Workers Employment, accommodation and meal conditions must be specified.

This contract meets most basic requirements of the Labor Standards Act, but attention is needed due to several important omissions.

The omission of probationary period is an important matter related to wage deduction. According to Labor Standards Act Article 17, the probationary period must be specified in the employment contract, and omitting this may result in workers working under different conditions than expected.

The omission of break time directly affects the protection of workers' rights. Labor Standards Act Article 54 requires guaranteeing at least 30 minutes of break time for 4 or more hours of work, and failure to specify this may result in insufficient rest during actual work.

For foreign workers, accommodation type and meal cost conditions are important working conditions. According to the Act on Foreign Workers Employment, these conditions must be clearly specified, and omission can cause disputes.

Fortunately, minimum wage standards are met, so there are no serious legal violations, but the above omissions need to be addressed to create a more complete contract.
The employment contract has a basic framework but may have issues with worker rights protection due to unclear probationary period and wage payment conditions.
Annual paid leave conditions not specified
According to Labor Standards Act Article 2-2, probationary period cannot exceed 3 months and must be specified in the contract.
According to Labor Standards Act Article 43, wages must be paid in full and directly to workers in currency, and payment method must be clearly specified.
According to Labor Standards Act Article 60, 15 days of paid leave must be granted to workers who attended 80% or more for one year.

This contract follows the basic structure of the Labor Standards Act, but attention is needed due to unclear parts in several items important for worker rights protection.

The non-specification of probationary period is a serious problem. According to Labor Standards Act Article 2-2, probationary period is limited to a maximum of 3 months, and wage reduction is possible during this period, so it must be specified in the contract. If probationary period is not specified, workers may face unexpected wage reduction.

Unclear wage payment method is also problematic. Labor Standards Act Article 43 stipulates paying wages in full and directly to workers in currency, and unclear payment method risks wage arrears or improper deductions.

Non-specification of annual paid leave conditions affects workers' right to rest. Annual paid leave under Labor Standards Act Article 60 is a basic right of workers, so failure to specify this may prevent proper vacation use in actual work.

Overall, this contract does not seriously violate legal standards, but the above items need to be supplemented for worker protection.
The employment contract has multiple serious legal violations including minimum wage violation, excessive working hours, and unspecified probationary period requiring immediate correction.
Below minimum wage (8,500 won per hour)
According to the Minimum Wage Act, 2024 minimum wage of 9,860 won or more must be paid, but the contract specifies 8,500 won, which is a legal violation.
According to Labor Standards Act Article 50, daily 8 hours and weekly 40 hours cannot be exceeded, but 13-hour work is a serious violation.
According to Labor Standards Act Article 2-2, probationary period must be specified and cannot exceed 3 months maximum.

This contract seriously violates the Labor Standards Act and is at a dangerous level requiring immediate correction.

The most serious problem is minimum wage violation. Specifying 8,500 won compared to the 2024 minimum wage of 9,860 won is a clear violation of the Minimum Wage Act, and employers can face up to 3 years imprisonment or fines up to 20 million won. Workers can claim damages for unpaid wages.

Excessive 13-hour daily working hours is also a very serious problem. Labor Standards Act Article 50 sets 8 hours daily and 40 hours weekly as basic working hours, and cannot exceed 52 hours weekly including extended work. 13-hour work greatly violates this and can pose serious risks to worker health and safety.

Non-specification of probationary period is an important matter related to wage reduction. According to Labor Standards Act Article 2-2, probationary period must be specified and cannot exceed 3 months.

These violations can cause particularly serious harm to foreign workers and require labor office reporting or legal action. Contract conditions must be immediately corrected to meet legal standards.
